VM3 - Arbitrary Data.vi

Owning Palette: Variable Manager

Manages VarMan variables of an arbitrary data type; both predefined and user-defined data types are supported. This VI provides the Writer ID functionality.

Details

Click the parameters for more information

 

cmd (read) specifies the operation to execute:

0createcreates a variable
1destroydestroys a variable
2writewrites a variable value
3readreads the variable value (default operation)
VC Handle specifies the handle of the Variable Context in which to operate on the variable. To operate on a global variable, pass -1 to this input. VC Handle is ignored if name_spec refers to the variable by an alias. See the Referring to variables topic for more information.
The VM - Open Context.vi creates a Variable Context and returns its handle.
name_spec defines the name specifier of the target variable. Usually, this is merely a variable name; however, additional options are available. See the Referring to variables topic for details.
flattened value in specifies the value to be written to the variable; it is only used if cmd (read) is either write or create. Values of all data types are presented in the Flattened-To-String format, with the exception of the String type.
writer ID specifies the Writer ID for the input value. It is only used during the write or the create operations.
error in describes error conditions that occur before this VI runs. This input provides standard error in functionality.
status indicates error status.
code contains error code.
source contains additional error information.
var type in specifies the data type code of the target variable. VarMan strictly enforces data type codes. However, an application can pass -1 to this input to read a variable value of an arbitrary data type, in which case var type out returns the actual data type code. Passing a data type code of -1 during write or create operations will cause the VI to return an error.
dup name_spec is a flow-through parameter with the same value as name_spec.
flattened value out returns the value that was read from the variable. Values of all data types are presented in the Flattened-To-String format, with the exception of the String type.
stats returns information about the most recent value of the variable.
writer ID indicates the Writer ID for the most recent value.
write MS indicates the Milliseconds Timer value (the output of the Tick Count (ms) primitive) when the variable value was written.
write TS indicates the time stamp (DBL representation), in the universal LabVIEW date/time format, when the variable value was written.
write Cnt indicates the variable's write counter. This counter starts at zero (0) when the variable is created and increments every time the variable is written.
error out contains error information. This output provides standard error out functionality.
status indicates error status.
code contains VarMan VI error code identifying an error if any occurred. If no error occurred, it is equal to zero.
source contains the error description and VI location information if an error occurred.
var type out returns the actual data type code.

 

VM3 - Arbitrary Data.vi - details

The VI accepts and returns variable values in the Flattened-To-String format, with the exception of the String type, whose values are passed as native LabVIEW strings. For predefined data types, the VI checks the consistency of the data type code and value format, and it returns an error in case of a mismatch.

Also see VarMan overview.
